text:
alex: Heads-up — after the canary yesterday we triggered an epoch resync that surfaced a few subtle eviction/handshake problems. Dropping notes + a short operator playbook so we have something repeatable.

sam: TL;DR what happened?

alex: During a prefetched-lease epoch handoff a node restarted mid-demote. Some eviction tokens for epoch N were partially applied, then another replica resumed with epoch N+1 and attempted a resync; a subset of prefixes ended up getting double-evicted and the residency counters were inconsistent for ~45s. We saw a spike in 409s and degraded cold-read tails.

jin: Oof. Invariant break or just telemetry/ops noise?

alex: Mostly ops noise but two concrete bugs: 1) residency counters temporarily went negative in the aggregate (we're not protecting the decrement path), and 2) eviction telemetry doesn't include a globally-unique token id so duplicates are invisible in metrics.

maya: What did you do to stabilize?

alex: Quick mitigation sequence we ran: pause the resync cron on cluster-B, run the idempotent reconciliation job against the lease log to rebuild residency counters, apply a short safety fence that blocks commits for epochs < observed_head for 30s, and clear soft-evict markers where reconciler determined they were applied twice.

sam: Could the handshake be made safer so partial applies don't lead to double-evict?

jin: Proposal: convert epoch resync to a two-phase protocol — prepare (dry-run) which computes diffs and checks CAS-able token state, then commit which performs a CAS on a per-prefix eviction-token record. That way partial apply can't silently double-apply. Also embed a sequence/UUID in each eviction token.

alex: Agreed. Also add an out-of-band admin reconcile endpoint: `/admin/kv/resync?dry=true` that returns a summary of diffs without applying them. Useful for ops drills.

maya: Add telemetry: emit {evict_token_uuid, epoch, node_id, prefix_count} and a counter for duplicate-apply attempts so we can alert on >0 duplicates in canary.

ci-bot: deploy:epoch-resync-reconcile v1.2 deployed to canary — checks passed (build 4821).

sam: We should codify an operator playbook. Quick draft that worked for us?

alex: Pasting the short playbook we used: 

```
1) Pause resync cron on affected cluster: `./infractl resync pause --cluster B`
2) Run reconcile (dry run first): `./tools/kv-resync --cluster B --dry-run > /tmp/resync-diff.json`
3) Inspect diffs, then run: `./tools/kv-resync --cluster B --apply --concurrency 20`
4) If negative residency counts observed, run counter-rebuild: `./tools/residency-rebuild --source lease-log --cluster B`
5) Re-enable resync after metrics stable for 5m: `./infractl resync resume --cluster B`
6) File followups: bug for negative-decrement, RFC for two-phase-resync, metrics ticket for duplicate token id.
```

jin: Add a note to temporarily route cold reads to shadow readpath during reconcile if counters look off — reduces 409 noise.

maya: Who picks up the RFC + fix tickets?

sam: I'll own the RFC for two-phase resync. Assign jin as reviewer and alex for ops integration.

alex: I'll open bugs for the negative-counter path and telemetry improvements today.

maya: :thumbsup: Also let's add a canary gate that fails build if duplicate-apply metric spikes during canary rollout.

ci-bot: alert rule added: `kv.eviction.duplicate_apply > 0` in canary -> notify #eng-oncall.

sam: Good. Follow-ups: RFC (sam) -> due EOW, bug tickets (alex) -> EOD, canary alert (mike) to confirm but ci-bot shows rule added.

alex: Thanks team — I'll post the short postmortem and link the tickets once created.

maya: Thanks — super useful to have the playbook.

alex: Done: opened tickets 6789 (neg-counter), 6790 (telemetry token id), RFC 6801 (two-phase resync).
